prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell); normalizes each Flight Intent Message against Airport Capacity Plan. Proposes TOBT (Target Off Block Time) only if airside capacity and ground service path allow; conditional if handling resources arrive after ready time; frozen at horizon unless rule exception or authorized override is recorded. Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. Parts: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; demand by stand, apron, runway, departure fix); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; compares demand with Airport Acceptance Rate (AAR), runway configuration, taxiway, sector limits; restriction = time-bounded throughput reduction; recalculates AAR on late reduction); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; derives CTT, Calculated Takeoff Time; revises only within authority/fairness rules; shall adjust departure times when metering needs stand absorption); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; derives TOBT protecting CTT, converts runway demand to stand delay, prefers stand absorption without gate conflict; sends CTT to TSM; pushback windows are narrow bands, not clearances); North Runway Meter and South Runway Meter (independent queue counts); Surface Surveillance Adapter (confirms holding-point counts); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; Common Situation Display; frozen change needs revised reason code; shall publish tower readiness changes within refresh interval); Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; refreshes advisories on restriction changes); Arrival Regulation Console; Sector Load Monitor; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; routes alerts by role via BRR); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; produces Fuel Truck Hold Advice); Collaborative Decision Log; Performance Analytics Warehouse (compares planned capacity, alerts, acknowledgements, realized delay); Handling Resource Planner (HRP; Stand Tow Request Form); Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Business Rules Registry (BRR); Audit Event Ledger; Identity Access Service; Digital Briefing Room. Modes: Normal Operations; Adverse Weather Mode/Capacity Reduction State; Recovery Phase. Actors: Regional Flow Manager (Copperfin; Ground Delay Program, metering/delay/reroute choices); Slot Coordinator (Halcyon; records pushback window rationale in coordination notes before release); Airline Operations Coordinator (AOC, Saffron); Aircraft Operator Representative (AOR); Ground Handling Dispatcher; Ramp Control Lead (accepts windows); Tower Supervisor (monitors release rate);

Document units:
S362: The Airline Operations Coordinator confirms whether each affected aircraft can absorb the assigned delay at stand without compromising crew, passenger, or turnaround constraints.
S363: If an operator cannot accept the proposed stand delay, the Aircraft Operator Representative requests reconsideration through the Airport CDM Portal.
S364: The Gate Conflict Detector warns when continued stand holding would block an inbound allocation or create a conflict with a planned equipment move.
S365: Business Rules Registry parameters define the maximum planned runway queue, the warning threshold, and the intervention threshold for each runway configuration.
S366: When a predicted queue exceeds the warning threshold, the Alert Distribution Hub highlights the affected runway queue on the Common Situation Display.
S367: During Adverse Weather Mode, the Regional Flow Manager may increase stand absorption to prevent unstable taxi queues from forming under reduced visibility or wet surface conditions.
S368: In a Capacity Reduction State, the Airport Duty Manager and Tower Supervisor agree whether the metering horizon should be extended so that delay is absorbed before pushback rather than near the runway.
S369: All changes to Target Off Block Time values, Calculated Takeoff Time values, and threshold overrides are written to the Collaborative Decision Log and Audit Event Ledger.
S370: The Performance Analytics Warehouse later compares planned stand absorption, actual off block performance, and runway queue length to verify that the agreed thresholds were not exceeded.
S371: The Regional Flow Platform enters the winter operating mode when freezing precipitation, contamination reports, or low surface temperature forecasts make untreated ground movement unreliable.
S372: The Meteorology Briefing Officer confirms the trigger conditions in the Digital Briefing Room so that airport, airline, and tower participants share one operational assumption.
S373: In this mode, the Capacity Assessment Module reduces practical departure capacity to account for deicing time, pad transit time, and slower ramp taxi speeds.
S374: The Airport Capacity Plan is revised with a winter margin before the Slot Allocation Engine recalculates affected Calculated Takeoff Time values.
S375: The Deicing Coordinator maintains the active pad configuration, including open bays, closed bays, fluid limitations, and vehicle availability.
S376: Pad queue controls assign aircraft to a deicing lane only after the Target Off Block Time is stable enough to support a realistic treatment sequence.
S377: The Ramp Movement Board displays each aircraft as pending push, taxi to pad, in treatment, awaiting release, or returning to stand when treatment cannot be completed.
